stories.title: Ghana Judicial Service holds talks to prevent staff strike
stories.summary: The Judicial Service has met staff unions over outstanding pay and working-condition concerns in an effort to prevent a resumption of industrial action. Management says it has asked government stakeholders for urgent discussions.

stories.title: Ghana’s energy minister presents new petroleum authority bill
stories.summary: Energy Minister John Jinapor has laid the National Petroleum Authority Bill 2026 before Parliament. The proposed legislation seeks to update and consolidate rules governing Ghana’s downstream petroleum industry.

stories.title: Ghana Airports Company funds 10 sniffer dogs for airport security
stories.summary: Ghana Airports Company has funded the purchase of 10 sniffer dogs for the Narcotics Control Commission. The dogs are expected to support drug detection and help address security gaps at the country’s airports.

stories.title: University of Ghana seeks legal clarity on rent rules for student hostels
stories.summary: The University of Ghana has asked for clarification on whether existing rent legislation applies to accommodation operated by its enterprise company. The university says it reduced a proposed increase for standard four-bed rooms from 26% to 15% after student consultations.

stories.title: Burkina Faso court clerk remanded over alleged CFA4.5m auction fraud
stories.summary: A court clerk in Bobo-Dioulasso has been placed in custody over allegations that he collected CFA4.5 million by promising a vehicle auction that prosecutors say was fictitious. The case is being handled by the local prosecutor’s office.

stories.title: Burkina Faso arbitration centre seeks easier dispute resolution for SMEs
stories.summary: The Ouagadougou Centre for Arbitration, Mediation and Conciliation has urged wider use of mediation and arbitration by small businesses. The centre says accessible dispute-resolution options can reduce legal costs and help protect commercial relationships.

stories.title: Burkina Faso groups strengthen citizen oversight of local budgets
stories.summary: A public-finance research centre is supporting citizen committees in Korsimoro and Ziniaré to track municipal revenue, spending and projects. The initiative aims to give residents a stronger voice in local budget decisions and public investment.

stories.title: Burkina Faso bids farewell to Iran’s ambassador after three-year mission
stories.summary: Burkina Faso’s foreign minister has received Iran’s outgoing ambassador, reviewing more than three years of bilateral cooperation. Officials highlighted diplomatic exchanges and joint initiatives during the envoy’s tenure.

stories.title: Ghana lifts Nkwanta South curfew but keeps weapons ban
stories.summary: Ghana has lifted the curfew in 11 communities in Nkwanta South after authorities reported an improved security situation. The ban on carrying arms and other offensive weapons remains in force across the municipality.

stories.title: Ghana estimates 5.4 million people still practise open defecation
stories.summary: Ghana’s Local Government Ministry says about 5.4 million people still practise open defecation. The deputy minister highlighted sanitation risks for women and girls and called for more investment in household and public toilet facilities.

stories.title: GRA identifies VAT compliance breaches at 14 Achimota businesses
stories.summary: The Ghana Revenue Authority says inspections at Achimota Retail Centre found issues including unauthorised invoice systems and failures to issue VAT invoices. The authority says enforcement checks will continue and businesses found in breach may face penalties.

stories.title: Ghana and Norway announce new support for startups and fintech firms
stories.summary: Ghana’s foreign minister says new cooperation with Norway will support startups and small businesses, offer investment packages for fintech firms and assist a local green-cement producer. The partnership is also expected to cover ethical AI and scholarships.

stories.title: Ghana launches diaspora trade conference to attract investment
stories.summary: The Diaspora Affairs Office has launched a trade conference scheduled for January 5 to connect Ghanaians abroad with investment opportunities and help local small businesses reach export markets.

stories.title: Ghana energy group urges review of fuel-marking costs
stories.summary: The Centre for Environmental Management and Sustainable Energy has urged Parliament to reassess the cost of the fuel-marking programme as it considers the National Petroleum Authority Bill. The group says newer monitoring technology may reduce duplication and costs.

stories.title: Burkina Faso plans CFA104bn modern market project in two cities
stories.summary: The government plans to invest about CFA104.4 billion in the RAAGA project to build modern market complexes in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso. Planned facilities include shops, food areas, parking, health and administrative services.

stories.title: Burkina Faso and Mali agree cross-border water roadmap for 2027–2029
stories.summary: Officials from Burkina Faso and Mali have adopted a three-year roadmap to improve the joint management of shared water resources. Priorities include climate and hydrological data sharing, pollution prevention and early warning for floods and droughts.

stories.title: Burkina Faso chamber of commerce visits Bobo-Dioulasso factories
stories.summary: The Chamber of Commerce and Industry has visited several processing businesses in Bobo-Dioulasso to understand their operating challenges. Companies raised issues including finance, energy costs, raw-material supply and logistics while showcasing local maize, cashew, cotton and textile production.

stories.title: Burkina Faso announces major military parade for December 11 celebration
stories.summary: Burkina Faso says its December 11 national celebration in Ouagadougou will include a major military parade. Regional organising committees have also been established as part of preparations for the event.

stories.title: Itel Energy opens first showroom in Burkina Faso
stories.summary: Itel Energy has opened its first Ouagadougou showroom, offering lithium batteries and inverters for homes, shops and industrial users. The distributor says the outlet will provide product guidance and after-sales support.

stories.title: Kenya targets January 2027 release of KCSE examination results
stories.summary: Kenya’s education ministry says marking of the 2026 KCSE scripts will begin promptly, with about 34,170 examiners expected at 41 centres. More than one million candidates sat the national examination.

stories.title: Kenya’s 2026 KCSE examinations conclude after final physics paper
stories.summary: The final Physics Practical paper brought the 2026 Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education examinations to a close. More than 1.04 million candidates completed the assessment across 10,693 examination centres.

stories.title: Governance and interoperability gaps slow Kenya’s instant-payment ambitions
stories.summary: A 2026 AfricaNenda report says Kenya’s PesaLink and mobile-money systems still face governance, interoperability and consumer-protection gaps. The report calls for stronger participation and more integrated payment infrastructure.

stories.title: Kenyan court clears extradition of murder suspect to the UK
stories.summary: A Nairobi court has ruled that legal requirements have been met for Brian Kiprop Kiplagat’s extradition to the United Kingdom. He will remain in custody pending surrender, subject to a 15-day appeal window.

stories.title: South Africa courts Silicon Valley investors and targets 3% economic growth
stories.summary: South Africa's government news agency reports that President Cyril Ramaphosa is courting Silicon Valley investors as the country pursues a 3% economic-growth target. The outreach forms part of efforts to attract investment and strengthen the country's technology and innovation sectors.

stories.title: ANC and smaller parties near Johannesburg coalition deal that could sideline DA
stories.summary: Reuters reports that the ANC and several smaller parties are close to a coalition agreement in Johannesburg after local elections produced no outright majority. The proposed arrangement could exclude the Democratic Alliance despite it winning the largest share of votes, raising questions about municipal stability and service delivery.

stories.title: South African Reserve Bank keeps key interest rate at 7.25% in split vote
stories.summary: Reuters reports that the Reserve Bank held its policy rate at 7.25%, with four of seven monetary-policy committee members supporting a pause and three favouring an increase. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said policymakers would act if inflation risks materialise.

stories.title: South African rand approaches one-year low as coalition uncertainty weighs
stories.summary: Reuters reports that the rand fell to a one-year low as uncertainty over local coalition negotiations and a stronger US dollar pressured the currency. A divided central-bank decision to hold interest rates also weighed on sentiment.

stories.title: Four killed in minibus and truck collision near Enfidha in Tunisia
stories.summary: The Tunisia Press executive news report says four people were killed and others injured when a minibus and a truck collided near Enfidha in Sousse Governorate. The incident renews attention on road safety and emergency response.

stories.title: Algerian man sentenced in France over multiple false identity-document applications
stories.summary: Algérie 360 reports that a 40-year-old Algerian man was sentenced in Lyon to six months in prison after applying for identity documents under different names in six French departments. The case concerns document fraud in France and is included as a diaspora-related legal story.

stories.title: Libyan investigation into migrant's torture death uncovers 483 Eritreans near Tripoli
stories.summary: Libya Review reports that an investigation following the alleged torture death of an Eritrean migrant uncovered 483 Eritreans held at a site south of Tripoli. Prosecutors reportedly opened an investigation and a suspected trafficker was arrested; the allegations underscore the risks faced by migrants in Libya.

stories.title: Tunisia cancels planned three-day fuel-transport strike
stories.summary: The General Federation of Petroleum and Chemical Products has called off a fuel-transport strike that had been scheduled for November 23–25. The union cited initial steps to regularise workers' social-security coverage, while saying it will continue to press for outstanding commitments.

stories.title: Tunisian young doctors suspend planned strike after overdue payments begin
stories.summary: The Tunisian Organisation of Young Doctors suspended a strike planned for November 20 after receiving reports that overdue payments had started reaching staff at several hospitals. The organisation says the arrears also affect 15 other university hospitals and warns that wider action remains possible if payments stall.

stories.title: Egypt and Libya sign agreements on gas, refining, fisheries and labour
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi and Libyan Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh witnessed agreements covering natural-gas infrastructure, petroleum refining, fisheries, labour, research and small businesses. The two governments also agreed to work on visa, residency and border-entry issues affecting Libyan citizens in Egypt.

stories.title: Benin directs most new primary-education funding to school meals
stories.summary: Benin's proposed 2027 primary-education budget would direct about 82% of its planned increase to school canteens. The proposal includes expanded meal coverage, with the government aiming to reach 1.9 million pupils; parliament is still reviewing the budget.

stories.title: Burkina Faso plans Perkoa zinc mine restart with CFA37bn investment
stories.summary: Burkina24 reports a planned restart of the Perkoa zinc mine backed by an investment of CFA37 billion. The development is a significant mining and employment story for the country's industrial sector.

stories.title: Burundi arrests of Banyamulenge refugees raise rights concerns
stories.summary: SOS Médias Burundi reports that more than 25 Banyamulenge refugees have been arrested since October amid a wider wave of detentions. The report raises questions about refugee protection and due process.

stories.title: Cabo Verde court publishes notice in Ivo Monteiro Andrade case
stories.summary: Mindel Insite carries a public court notice from the Barlavento Court of Appeal concerning a special action involving Ivo Monteiro Andrade. The notice is part of the day's legal and public-record reporting from Cabo Verde.

stories.title: Côte d’Ivoire, Benin and Togo agree on gas-supply security
stories.summary: Linfodrome reports that Côte d’Ivoire, Benin and Togo have signed a protocol aimed at securing their gas supplies. The agreement highlights regional energy cooperation and the importance of reliable fuel infrastructure.

stories.title: Guinea's Doumbouya asks ministers to account for their work on state television
stories.summary: Guinee7 reports that President Mamadi Doumbouya has asked ministers to publicly report on their management through national broadcaster RTG. The move places government performance and public accountability in the spotlight.

stories.title: Liberian diaspora voting campaign gains momentum ahead of 2029 elections
stories.summary: FrontPage Africa reports that a campaign to expand voting participation among Liberians living abroad is gaining momentum, with a Columbus discussion led by Professors Quioh and Redd. The issue is part of wider debate about diaspora participation in national elections.

stories.title: Worker dies after fatal workplace incident at Mauritania construction site
stories.summary: Sahara Medias reports that a worker died following an incident involving a colleague at a construction site in Zouerate. Authorities and investigators will need to establish the circumstances surrounding the fatal event.

stories.title: Niger holds briefing on China's policy decisions and bilateral relations
stories.summary: Le Sahel reports on a press briefing examining the Chinese Communist Party's latest central committee decisions and their possible implications for China–Niger relations. The discussion reflects the continuing diplomatic and economic links between the two countries.

stories.title: Senegal prosecutor seeks trial of six suspects in Aziz Dabala and Wally Gano murder case
stories.summary: Dakaractu reports that prosecutors have requested that six people be sent before a criminal court over the 2024 killings of Aziz Dabala and Wally Gano. The investigating judge must still decide whether to order a trial; one accused person disputes the allegations.

stories.title: Togo opposition movement promotes SIKA in debate over monetary sovereignty
stories.summary: Icilome reports that the DMK movement is backing SIKA as part of its proposal for monetary sovereignty in Togo. The story adds to the country's ongoing public debate about currency, economic independence and regional monetary arrangements.

stories.title: Angolan civic group reports imbalance in public-media coverage
stories.summary: The civic movement MUDEI says its six-month monitoring found that 60–70% of airtime in the outlets it reviewed went to the Executive, with the ruling MPLA receiving most party coverage. The report renews debate about media pluralism and public broadcasting ahead of 2027 elections.

stories.title: Cameroonian rights lawyer urges Biya to release Nera 10 and other detainees
stories.summary: Mimi Mefo Info reports that lawyer Agbor Balla has urged President Paul Biya to release the Nera 10 and other people detained in connection with the Anglophone crisis. The appeal keeps attention on detention, dialogue and the long-running conflict in Cameroon's English-speaking regions.

stories.title: Death of Zémio trader in Central African Republic military prison prompts concern
stories.summary: Corbeau News reports that a trader from Zémio died while detained at Camp de Roux military prison, with the outlet noting several detainee deaths over the past month. The circumstances require transparent investigation and independent scrutiny.

stories.title: Chadian university researchers earn CAMES academic promotions
stories.summary: Alwihda Info reports that several teacher-researchers from Chad have earned agrégation qualifications through the 2026 CAMES competition. The achievement highlights academic development and regional higher-education cooperation.

stories.title: Congo report highlights digital platforms as opportunity for postal services
stories.summary: Vox Congo examines how digital platforms could support the postal sector in the Republic of the Congo. The report points to technology as a possible route to modernising services and responding to changing customer needs.

stories.title: DR Congo certifies nearly $154m in oil-sector losses and shortfalls over three months
stories.summary: Radio Okapi reports that authorities have certified close to US$154 million in losses and shortfalls in the petroleum sector over a three-month period. The figures raise questions about oil-sector accounting, public revenue and oversight.

stories.title: Journalists from several countries receive Honest View 2026 awards in Moscow
stories.summary: Real Equatorial Guinea reports that journalists from different countries have received the 2026 Honest View awards in Moscow. The recognition puts international media work and cross-border journalism in focus.

stories.title: Gabon receives 37,600 day-old chicks for poultry production
stories.summary: Agence Gabonaise de Presse reports that 37,600 day-old chicks have arrived in Libreville under the POUFA livestock programme. The delivery is intended to support poultry production and the domestic food supply.

stories.title: São Tomé residents call for concrete answers from the new government
stories.summary: Téla Nón reports that citizens are waiting for practical responses from the country's new executive. The story reflects public expectations around delivery, governance and the priorities of the new administration.

stories.title: African instant payments reach $1.8tn as trust gaps slow the shift away from cash
stories.summary: Capital Ethiopia reports that instant-payment transactions across Africa have reached about US$1.8 trillion, while gaps in trust and adoption still limit the move away from cash. The findings point to the importance of interoperable, secure digital-payment systems.

stories.title: Kenyan opposition leaders walk out of IEBC talks over 2027 election preparations
stories.summary: Opposition leaders left a consultative meeting with Kenya's electoral commission, accusing it of sidelining them and failing to act on earlier reform proposals. The IEBC says it is prepared to explain its work, while disputes over voter registers, tallying and election readiness continue.

stories.title: Madagascar Ambohimalaza case: civil party seeks testimony from former health minister
stories.summary: 2424.mg reports that the civil party in the Ambohimalaza case is asking for the former health minister and intensive-care doctors to appear. The legal proceedings continue as families seek answers about the case.

stories.title: Malawi former police informant publicly challenges officers over alleged mistreatment
stories.summary: Malawi24 reports on a former police informant who has turned against officers, using the words “I'm coming, kill me” in a confrontation. The account raises questions about police conduct and the safety of people who previously worked with law enforcement.

stories.title: Rwanda argues Francophone institutions should not be controlled by former colonial powers
stories.summary: KT Press commentary argues that the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie should remain an association of sovereign states rather than an extension of any one country's foreign policy. The piece reflects Rwanda's position in a wider debate about African agency and international partnerships.

stories.title: European Union delegation makes courtesy visit in Seychelles
stories.summary: Seychelles Broadcasting Corporation reports on a courtesy visit by a European Union delegation. The engagement is a small but relevant diplomatic update as the island nation maintains ties with international partners.

stories.title: Somalia's prime minister accuses UAE of funding conflict in South West State
stories.summary: Goobjoog reports that Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre has accused the United Arab Emirates of funding conflicts in Somalia's South West State. The allegation adds to diplomatic tensions and debate over foreign involvement in Somalia's internal affairs.

stories.title: Twenty-nine Juba prison inmates, including four on death row, sit CPE examinations
stories.summary: Eye Radio reports that 29 inmates at Juba prison, including four prisoners on death row, are sitting CPE examinations. The development highlights access to education for people in detention.

stories.title: Sudan armed group claims control of Bau area in Blue Nile region
stories.summary: Radio Dabanga reports that the Tasis forces have announced control of the Bau area in Blue Nile state. The claim comes amid continuing conflict; independent confirmation of territorial control is not established by the headline alone.

stories.title: East African Community urged to shield regional economies from global shocks
stories.summary: Tanzania's Daily News reports calls for the East African Community to strengthen its resilience against global economic shocks. The discussion focuses on protecting regional economies and improving cooperation as external pressures shift.

stories.title: Slaty egret offers researchers a clue to the health of Botswana's Okavango Delta
stories.summary: Weekend Post reports on the slaty egret as a possible indicator of ecological conditions in the Okavango Delta. The story highlights the role of wildlife observation in understanding wetland health and conservation needs.

stories.title: Eswatini anti-corruption commission arrests police officer in reconstruction-fund fraud case
stories.summary: The Eswatini Observer reports that the Anti-Corruption Commission has arrested a police officer in connection with alleged fraud involving the E960,000 Reconstruction Fund. The case raises questions about public-fund oversight and accountability.

stories.title: Lesotho report calls on men and boys to help end menstrual-health stigma
stories.summary: Newsday Lesotho examines how men and boys can support menstrual health and help challenge stigma. The report highlights education, open discussion and shared responsibility in improving menstrual-health awareness.

stories.title: Mozambique opposition demands inquiry into suspected mining-related water pollution
stories.summary: Renamo has renewed its call for a parliamentary inquiry into alleged oil and fuel pollution in rivers in Moma and Larde districts. The party says communities depend on the affected water sources; parliament's standing commission is expected to respond.

stories.title: Namibian court imposes 30-year prison term in child-rape case
stories.summary: New Era reports that a court has sentenced a child-rape offender to 30 years in prison, describing the crime as a grave violation of the victim's personhood. The ruling underscores the seriousness with which the court treated the offence.

stories.title: Zambia police discipline officers over handling of fatal crash involving district commissioner
stories.summary: Zambia Monitor reports that police have disciplined officers over their handling of an accident that claimed the life of a district commissioner. The case has prompted scrutiny of police procedures and accountability.

stories.title: Speeding blamed in death of six-year-old girl in Zimbabwe's Bulawayo
stories.summary: CITE reports that speeding has been blamed for the death of a six-year-old girl in Bulawayo. The incident renews attention on road safety, responsible driving and protection of children on public roads.

stories.title: Two hippos in Kenya die after eating maize and fishing nets, report says
stories.summary: Daily Maverick reports that two hippos died after eating maize and fishing nets. The incident raises concerns about human activity, waste and wildlife health in shared ecosystems.

stories.title: Egypt says it repaid $38.2bn in external debt amid record foreign reserves
stories.summary: Egypt Independent reports that Egypt has repaid US$38.2 billion in external debt while foreign-exchange reserves reached a record level. The figures come amid continuing scrutiny of the country's external financing and debt position.

stories.title: Morocco's Friday press review tracks the day's national headlines
stories.summary: Hespress has published its November 20 press review, bringing together a selection of current stories covered by Moroccan newspapers. This is a daily media roundup rather than a single new government decision.

stories.title: Tunisia court sentences former IVD head Sihem Ben Sedrine to five years
stories.summary: Mosaique FM reports that former Truth and Dignity Commission head Sihem Ben Sedrine has received a five-year prison sentence in the IVD case. The development is significant for Tunisia's transitional-justice debate.

stories.title: Markram to captain South Africa in second Test against Bangladesh
stories.summary: Aiden Markram will lead South Africa in the second Test against Bangladesh, with the country's T20 and ODI squads also named. Reuters reported the selections as South Africa prepares for the next stage of its international cricket schedule.

stories.title: Wall Street futures slip as Anthropic shares retreat after market debut
stories.summary: US stock futures fell after Anthropic shares pulled back in premarket trading following a strong first day on the market. Reuters reported that concerns about AI-company valuations and signals from Federal Reserve officials also weighed on investor sentiment.

stories.title: Canada and Japan pursue new partnerships as global powers reshape diplomacy
stories.summary: Reuters reports that Canada and Japan are seeking wider trade, supply-chain and security partnerships as uncertainty grows around relations with Washington and Beijing. Canada advanced trade ties with the Philippines and ASEAN, while Japan pursued cooperation on critical minerals, energy and regional resilience.

stories.title: World Court finds Myanmar responsible for genocide against Rohingya
stories.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during the 2017 military campaign. The judgment, brought by The Gambia, is a landmark finding against a state and sets out obligations including reparations and the safe return of displaced people.

stories.title: APC campaign convoy attacked in Gombe after anti-party chants
stories.summary: A confrontation broke out in Kwarge, Balanga Local Government Area, after youths chanted an anti-APC slogan at a campaign convoy. Punch's morning report said buses were damaged and supporters injured; the incident adds to concerns about political violence ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.title: South Korea confirms first cholera case in a decade
stories.summary: South Korean health authorities have confirmed the country's first cholera case since 2016 in a patient who had not travelled overseas in the previous two months. Officials are tracing the possible source and contacts, and have advised people to use safe water and handle food carefully.

stories.title: FG suspends Lagos–Ibadan Expressway bridge work after 20-hour gridlock
stories.summary: The Federal Government suspended pedestrian-bridge construction at Aseese after a traffic diversion left motorists stranded for more than 20 hours. Traffic authorities said the suspension will remain in place pending fresh directions on the work and traffic arrangements.

stories.title: Osun police hunt suspects after mob kills rescued accident survivor in Ilesa
stories.summary: Police in Osun State say a man rescued after a crash that killed two pedestrians in Ilesa was later beaten by an angry mob and died in hospital. The command says the vehicle was burnt and has opened an investigation, warning residents against jungle justice.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill three in Kyiv and damage bridges and power infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian missiles and drones struck several Kyiv districts overnight, killing three people and injuring nine, according to local authorities cited by the Associated Press. The attacks damaged transport infrastructure and caused electricity disruptions, prompting officials to restrict traffic on affected bridges.

stories.title: FRSC records 941 road-crash deaths across Nigeria in third quarter
stories.summary: The Federal Road Safety Corps reported 941 deaths in 2,098 road crashes during the third quarter of 2026. Although deaths and crashes fell compared with the same period last year, the figures still represent more than ten road-crash deaths a day.

stories.title: Naira closes at ₦1,388 per dollar, its weakest level in eight months
stories.summary: The naira weakened at the official market on Thursday, closing at ₦1,388 per dollar, according to Central Bank trading data cited by Nairametrics. Interbank foreign-exchange turnover rose above $800 million, but increased trading activity did not prevent the currency from losing ground.

stories.title: ASUP orders strike across polytechnics in four South-West states
stories.summary: The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics has directed its chapters in Ogun, Oyo, Osun and Ekiti to continue industrial action over unpaid academic allowances and implementation of the 2025/2026 agreement. The union says Ondo is the only state in the zone to have implemented the relevant provisions.

stories.title: Gombe electricity transmission capacity doubles to 600MVA
stories.summary: A newly installed 300MVA transformer has doubled upstream capacity at the Gombe Transmission Substation from 300MVA to 600MVA. The Transmission Company of Nigeria says the upgrade is intended to strengthen supply infrastructure serving Gombe and neighbouring North-East states.

stories.title: Nigeria and Russia sign customs cooperation agreement to ease trade
stories.summary: The Nigeria Customs Service and Russia's Federal Customs Service have signed an agreement covering trade facilitation, intelligence sharing and customs enforcement. The two sides are also exploring mutual recognition arrangements for authorised economic operators.

stories.title: Glovo reports 230% rise in healthy-food orders across six African markets
stories.summary: Glovo says orders for healthy and high-protein food rose 230% across six African markets, including Nigeria. Its report says healthy meals account for 24% of orders on its Nigerian platform, reflecting growing demand for fresh produce and protein-rich options.

stories.title: Nigeria's daily petrol supply rises 21% to 46.9 million litres in October
stories.summary: Figures attributed to the NMDPRA show average daily petrol supply increased from 38.7 million litres in September to 46.9 million in October. The regulator's data also indicates that stock cover fell to 21.8 days, below the 30-day safety threshold.

stories.title: Federal Government advances plan to harmonise 2026 and 2027 budgets
stories.summary: The Federal Government is advancing plans to harmonise the 2026 and 2027 budgets to improve fiscal planning and make revenue and spending projections more realistic. The Economic Management Team also discussed food-price stability, energy coordination, tourism and the draft 2026–2036 National Development Plan.

stories.title: APGA endorses Tinubu as its preferred presidential candidate for 2027
stories.summary: Anambra Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented the APGA flag to President Bola Tinubu and named him the party's preferred candidate for the 2027 general election. Soludo urged people in the South-East to support the president's re-election bid.

stories.title: Myanmar rejects landmark ICJ genocide ruling as 'unfair'
stories.summary: Myanmar's government has rejected the International Court of Justice ruling that the state committed genocide against the Rohingya, calling the judgment unfair. The court's decision followed a case brought by The Gambia over the military's 2017 campaign; the ruling says Myanmar has obligations to provide reparations and enable safe return.

stories.title: COP31 climate talks enter final day amid dispute over fossil-fuel cuts
stories.summary: Negotiators at the UN climate summit in Antalya remain divided over stronger action to cut fossil-fuel use. A revised draft has removed explicit language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, while vulnerable countries say climate finance and disaster-recovery support remain inadequate.

stories.title: Xi projects China's global influence after hosting Trump and Putin at APEC
stories.summary: China's hosting of the APEC summit and a highly publicised meeting involving Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin has reinforced Beijing's image as a major diplomatic power broker. The talks produced no major breakthroughs, while trade and security questions remained unresolved.

stories.title: Nigeria energy brief: 300 CNG buses planned as oil derivation revenue falls
stories.summary: A November 20 energy roundup reports plans for 300 CNG buses, a fall in oil derivation receipts to producing states and a proposed sale of Shell's Daystar Power solar business. It also tracks regional energy developments, including Kenya's planned start of commercial oil production in December.

stories.title: SERAP gives INEC seven days to prosecute electoral violence suspects
stories.summary: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project has given INEC Chairman Professor Joash Amupitan seven days to prosecute suspects arrested over electoral and political violence, or face legal action. In a letter dated 14 November, SERAP asked the commission to obtain case files and investigation materials from the Nigeria Police Force and initiate prosecutions under the Electoral Act 2026. The demand follows reported incidents since 2027 campaign season began, including an attack on NDC members in Oregun, Lagos, on 12 November.

stories.title: Australia beat New Zealand 32-12 to win a fourth straight Rugby League World Cup
stories.summary: Australia defeated New Zealand 32-12 in the men’s Rugby League World Cup final at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane, leading 24-6 at halftime. It is Australia’s 13th world title from 17 tournaments and their fourth in succession, extending a run of 10 wins in the last 11 World Cups. Keaon Koloamatangi and Reece Walsh were among those celebrating after Jack Bostock crossed for a try.

stories.title: Kenya probes violent refugee protests at the Dadaab complex
stories.summary: Kenya’s Department of Refugee Services said protesters damaged its offices, stole government equipment and broke into nearby businesses during confrontations with security personnel at the Dadaab refugee complex. The unrest erupted on Saturday morning at the Hagadera camp in Garissa County after refugee youths opposed plans to build a modern market on an open field. Dadaab hosts more than 438,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, nearly 97% of them from Somalia, according to UNHCR.

stories.title: Cape Verde votes as President Neves seeks a second term
stories.summary: Cape Verdeans went to the polls on Sunday in a presidential election that pits incumbent Jose Maria Neves against five challengers, including former justice minister Joana Rosa, who is seeking to become the country's first female president. Neves, in office since 2021 and prime minister from 2001 to 2016, is favoured to win another five-year term. The vote is widely seen as a test of democratic stability in a region hit by coups elsewhere.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis in Khan Younis
stories.summary: Hamas confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, commander of its Rafah brigade in the al-Qassam Brigades, was killed in an Israeli air strike on the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis in southern Gaza. The 53-year-old had been a member of the armed wing since 1991 and Israel described him as a key planner of the October 7, 2023 attack. His funeral was held in Khan Younis on Sunday afternoon.

stories.title: 113th Grey Cup kicks off in Calgary as CFL crowns its champion
stories.summary: The 113th Grey Cup is being played at McMahon Stadium in Calgary, the sixth time the city has hosted the CFL championship and the first since 2019. The Montreal Alouettes clinched their place by beating the Winnipeg Blue Bombers in the East Division final. Sarah McLachlan performs the national anthem and Riley Green headlines the halftime show.

stories.title: IRGC says two oil tankers exploded on mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy said two oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming both vessels had switched off their navigation and AIS transponders to pass through an unauthorised route. The IRGC said two other tankers turned back after warnings from its maritime traffic control centre. US Central Command has not confirmed the Iranian account, and the reports could not be independently verified.

stories.title: Svitolina sets up WTA Finals title match against Andreeva at Indian Wells
stories.summary: Elina Svitolina reached the final of the 2026 WTA Finals at Indian Wells, where she will face Mirra Andreeva for the season-ending title. Svitolina, the 2018 champion, is playing the event for the first time since 2022, while Andreeva beat Jessica Pegula in the other semi-final to move one win from her first WTA Finals crown. The final closes the tournament on Sunday.

stories.title: Philippines and Australia sign defence pact as South China Sea tensions flare
stories.summary: Australia and the Philippines signed a major defence cooperation agreement on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila, expanding reciprocal military access, maritime awareness and information sharing. The deal is expected to bolster the Philippine Navy and coastguard and covers eight new defence infrastructure projects at five sites. Canberra and Manila have both faced repeated clashes with Chinese forces in the disputed waters.

stories.title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inducts Phil Collins, Oasis, Sade and Wu-Tang Clan
stories.summary: The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony was held on 14 November at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, honouring Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan. MC Lyte accepted the award for musical excellence, and Usher performed during the ceremony. ABC will broadcast the ceremony as a primetime special on 8 December, with Disney+ streaming it the following day.

stories.title: IRGC claims it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its aerospace forces struck and destroyed a US early-warning radar installation in Bahrain, describing the operation as retaliation for an air strike on a telecommunications tower in the port town of Sirik. The claim was carried by IRGC-affiliated media and has not been independently verified; neither Washington nor Manama commented immediately. Bahrain issued a second alert of a potential threat as the exchange widened beyond the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles toward Riyadh and drones over Eastern Province
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted and destroyed missiles launched toward Riyadh and drones over the kingdom’s Eastern Province. Spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said the coalition was responding to continued cross-border attacks as tensions with Yemen’s Houthi movement escalate. The coalition did not report casualties or damage in the latest interceptions.

stories.title: Academy holds 17th Governors Awards, honouring Close, Norman and Scott
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences holds its 17th Governors Awards on Sunday at the Ray Dolby Ballroom at Ovation Hollywood, the first major event of the awards season. Academy Honorary Awards go to actor Glenn Close, animator Floyd Norman and director Ridley Scott, with the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award to producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler. The honours are conferred by the Academy's Board of Governors rather than voted by members.

stories.title: Marcos opens 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila with 19 leaders expected
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr chaired the opening of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City. The three-day meeting under the theme 'Navigating Our Future, Together' covers regional security, economic resilience and the bloc's response to the crisis in Myanmar. Marcos is due to hand the ASEAN chairship to Singapore at the close.

stories.title: Notre Dame routs Boston College 41-7 in South Bend
stories.summary: Fifth-ranked Notre Dame beat Boston College 41-7 in the latest edition of the Holy War, with the Fighting Irish offence scoring on the ground and through the air. Boston College's lone score came on a third-quarter rushing touchdown by Bo MacCormack III, and defensive back KP Price recorded an interception and a sack. Notre Dame improved to 8-1 with the win.

stories.title: Svitolina sets up WTA Finals title match against Andreeva
stories.summary: Elina Svitolina dropped just three games against Linda Noskova to reach the FAGE WTA Finals championship match at Indian Wells, while Mirra Andreeva knocked out Jessica Pegula to reach her first final. Andreeva had already beaten Svitolina in straight sets during group play, saving all six break points she faced. The final pits the world number three against a former champion chasing her biggest title in years.

stories.title: Tinubu pledges to rebuild violence-ravaged Plateau communities
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu used a campaign stop in Jos to promise the reconstruction of communities displaced by years of violence in Plateau State. He said his administration's reforms were beginning to stabilise the economy and asked residents of the North-Central zone for a second term. Information Minister Mohammed Idris said the turnout reflected confidence in the government's programme.

stories.title: US air travel slowly recovers after nationwide ground stop, with 10,000 flights hit
stories.summary: Airlines cancelled more than 5,300 US flights and delayed almost 6,300 on Saturday, a day after about 9,200 were cancelled when the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop over disrupted air traffic communications. The FAA head predicted schedules would not return to normal until late Sunday, and the transportation secretary is seeking $50 billion to upgrade air traffic control.

stories.title: Portugal thrashed 4-1 by Denmark in first game since Ronaldo retired
stories.summary: Portugal lost 4-1 to Denmark in Braga in their first match since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring twice in eight minutes early in the second half. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg converted a penalty and Joachim Andersen headed a fourth before Bernardo Silva pulled one back in stoppage time. Every Portugal player and mascot wore 'Ronaldo 7' shirts in tribute before kick-off.

stories.title: Democrat Mary Peltola is likely to win Alaska’s US Senate race, NBC News projects
stories.summary: NBC News’ Decision Desk has characterised the Alaska Senate race as likely Democratic, with Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan trailing Peltola and both candidates below 50% of first-choice votes. The latest unofficial count from the Alaska Division of Elections put Peltola at 50.1%, more than 11,000 votes ahead, with ranked-choice tabulation due on 18 November. If she wins, Democrats would hold a 56-44 Senate majority next year.

stories.title: Nvidia investors urge board to weigh a return of Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker wrote to Nvidia's board urging a slow, measured and deliberate process on the company's future leadership, including the potential return of Jensen Huang. The letter did not call for his immediate reinstatement. Elon Musk said on X that he signed a petition backing Huang, which organisers say has more than 100,000 signatures including over 5,000 current Nvidia employees.

stories.title: France mobilises 70,000 police for fifth weekend of protests
stories.summary: Between 50 and 60 marches were expected across France as the 'Yellow Vests' coordination and student unions held a fifth consecutive weekend of demonstrations over the cost of living, education funding and a new police bill. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez mobilised around 70,000 police officers and gendarmes, with the Paris march running from Place de la Republique to Place de la Nation. The movement has produced thousands of arrests since it began in mid-October.

stories.title: Kremlin confirms Putin, Xi and Trump will meet in Shenzhen on 19 November
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said an agreement has been reached for Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump to hold a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on 19 November, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The White House confirmed Trump's attendance at the 18-19 November summit. It would be the first trilateral summit bringing together the leaders of the United States, Russia and China.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass in remote Andes town he once served
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV travelled by helicopter to Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, a town of about 5,000 people in the Andean highlands of the diocese where he served as bishop from 2015 to 2023. In his homily at an open-air Mass he praised the missionaries who evangelised the region and the popular piety of the high Andes. The visit is part of his apostolic journey through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

stories.title: South Africa pushes early diabetes detection on World Diabetes Day
stories.summary: Hundreds of Johannesburg residents received free blood pressure and diabetes screenings as South Africa marked World Diabetes Day under the theme 'Early action on diabetes'. Diabetes is the country's leading underlying natural cause of death, claiming nearly 29,000 lives a year, and roughly one in nine South African adults lives with the condition. The WHO says more than 40% of people with diabetes worldwide are undiagnosed.

stories.title: Philippines' Carmelle wins the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
stories.summary: Filipino singer Carmelle won the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok with a performance of her dance-pop song "Sobra-Sobra", taking 211 points. The 19-year-old beat 10 other acts in the grand final, with the result decided by national juries and viewers worldwide. A Thai duo finished second and Vietnam's Tóc Tiên third, as the 70-year-old contest expanded beyond Europe for the first time.

stories.title: Rubin Observatory spots dwarf planet candidate 2026 ED138 far beyond Pluto
stories.summary: The NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory has identified 2026 ED138, a large, bright trans-Neptunian object that the International Astronomical Union’s Minor Planet Center has flagged as a dwarf planet candidate. The object is currently about 46 times farther from the Sun than Earth and takes roughly 281 years to complete an orbit, on a path tilted nearly 25 degrees to the plane of the solar system. If confirmed, it would rank among the largest dwarf planets found in that region.

stories.title: SpaceX Starship returns to its Texas launch tower in first recovery of the spacecraft
stories.summary: SpaceX’s Starship came back from its longest flight in orbit yet and returned to the Texas launch tower it lifted off from a day earlier, the first key recovery of the rocket system’s centrepiece vessel. The flight was the 15th test of the two-stage vehicle and a milestone in the company’s decade-long effort to build a fully reusable rocket.

stories.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global 365 outage hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot
stories.summary: Microsoft apologised and said it had restored service after a global outage that disrupted Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Copilot for more than two workdays. Downdetector recorded reports from users in more than 70 countries, and governments, courts, hospitals, airlines and banks reported disruption. Microsoft said the incident stemmed from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade and was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.

stories.title: Wales stun New Zealand 35-28 for first win over All Blacks since 1953
stories.summary: Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 in Cardiff for their first victory over the All Blacks in 73 years, built on tries from Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit. Wales led 21-7 at half-time before New Zealand cut the gap to seven, and the hosts repelled wave after wave of attack to hold on. It is one of the biggest upsets of the autumn internationals.

stories.title: Tinubu breaks ground on $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu, represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, flagged off construction of the $3.5 billion Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State, a project delayed for years by political, legal and environmental disputes. The federal government said it completed environmental impact assessments and secured council approval with $2.27 billion in initial funding under a public-private partnership. Afreximbank is backing the project, which officials say will expand port capacity and support trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area.

stories.title: Hundreds march in Bangui over fuel prices and the detention of five activists
stories.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators took to the streets of the Central African Republic’s capital to protest fuel price rises and demand the release of five civil society leaders arrested after an October strike. Petrol now costs more than 1,100 CFA francs a litre, and the opposition coalition behind the march wants it cut to 850.

stories.title: Recording Academy sets 16 November for 2027 Grammy nominations
stories.summary: The Recording Academy will reveal nominees for the 69th Grammy Awards on Monday, 16 November, in a presentation streamed on Grammy.com and the Grammys YouTube channel with live coverage on Good Morning America. Pharrell Williams, Herbie Hancock, Kehlani, Olivia Dean, David Guetta and Ziggy Marley are among the artists announcing categories. The 2027 ceremony, set for 7 February, adds five new categories including best Asian pop music performance.

stories.title: Nigeria must clear 42 days of Ebola monitoring before being declared free
stories.summary: The WHO's executive director for health emergencies, Chikwe Ihekweazu, said Nigeria must monitor all 53 identified contacts of its imported Ebola case for 21 days and then a further 21 before it can be declared free of the disease. The NCDC had targeted 13 November to complete monitoring of 62 contacts linked to the case, a woman who travelled from Uganda and was later evacuated to Switzerland. Ihekweazu said the evacuation reflected the requesting country's wishes, not any gap in Nigerian capacity.

stories.title: Scientists find a simple route from spent coffee grounds to biodiesel
stories.summary: Researchers at Universitat Rovira i Virgili have identified the conditions for efficiently extracting oil from spent coffee grounds while preserving the remaining biomass for further processing. The extracted oil can serve as feedstock for biodiesel, while the residual lignocellulosic material can be converted into bioethanol, lactic acid and ingredients for sustainable aviation fuel. The work was published in a peer-reviewed journal and reported by ScienceDaily on 14 November.

stories.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran strikes unless Tehran provokes US
stories.summary: President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if Washington faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, according to three people familiar with the matter. Trump has alternated between threatening fresh strikes and signalling a wind-down, and officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind.

stories.title: Voyager 1 to become first human-made object one light-day from Earth
stories.summary: NASA says Voyager 1 will cross the one-light-day threshold on Wednesday, 18 November, at 5:16 a.m. EST, roughly 16 billion miles from Earth. The spacecraft, launched in 1977, will have taken 49 years, two months and 11 days to cover a distance light itself crosses in 24 hours. After that milestone a radio command takes about 24 hours to reach it, and a reply another 24 to return.

stories.title: Patriots and Lions meet in Munich as NFL returns to Germany
stories.summary: The New England Patriots (5-4) face the Detroit Lions (6-2) at FC Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena on Sunday in the NFL's Week 10 international game, the sixth regular-season game staged in Germany and the third in Munich. Detroit arrive on a four-game winning run knowing a victory would put them top of the NFC North. New England are coming off a 45-27 home defeat to Green Bay and have injury concerns, with A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson among those listed questionable.

stories.title: Lagos Art Week confronts history, identity and belonging at ART X Lagos
stories.summary: ART X Lagos, West Africa’s largest art fair, returned to the Federal Palace Hotel on Victoria Island as the centrepiece of Nigeria’s annual art week, with exhibitions, installations, music, talks and film screenings. This year’s edition, titled “A New Chapter, A New Decade”, explores how artists reinterpret heritage and identity.

stories.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over access to Android users' photos
stories.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta Platforms €805 million ($887 million) for using photos and videos from Android users' galleries on Facebook without specific consent or adequate disclosure. Investigators found the feature, which suggests gallery content for users to post, was enabled by default and covered by a single broad permission. Meta has 60 days to disable it by default and seek separate consent, and the company challenged Italy's jurisdiction.

stories.title: Microsoft apologises for global outage and rules out a cyberattack
stories.summary: Microsoft apologised after a global service disruption took down Teams, Outlook and Copilot for more than 24 hours across at least 70 countries, affecting government agencies, schools, airlines and hospitals. The company said the fault was introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and triggered by a subsequent network change, and that it found no indication of malicious activity or an AI cause. Service has since been restored, though Microsoft warned of intermittent issues.

stories.title: Zimbabwe's HIV gains face their hardest test among young people
stories.summary: Zimbabwe has exceeded the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets, with 97% of people living with HIV aware of their status, more than 95% on antiretroviral therapy and 96% of those virally suppressed. But critical gaps remain for children, adolescents and pregnant women, and nearly half of adolescents and young people are not in education, employment or training. Awareness of HIV status among young people in Harare rose from 63% to 85% between August 2025 and September 2026.

stories.title: Tinubu pledges to revive Nigeria's dormant refineries
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu has pledged to rehabilitate Nigeria's dormant national refineries, saying the facilities will not be allowed to become stranded investments as domestic refining capacity expands. Officials said Nigeria needs up to $40 billion in fresh oil and gas investment by 2030, and that talks with NNPC on a pilot national strategic stock programme are at an advanced stage. Import licences will stay open on published, merit-based criteria.

stories.title: South Sudan postpones first national elections to February 2027
stories.summary: South Sudan's National Election Commission published a revised timetable setting 11 February 2027 as polling day, replacing 22 December 2026, on the day voter registration was due to begin. The document gave no reason for the delay, which follows warnings from the South Sudan Civil Society Forum that conditions did not support fair and credible elections. The vote, the country's first since independence in 2011, has now been deferred repeatedly, including in 2022 and 2024.

stories.title: Uganda rejects al-Shabaab claims its soldiers were killed in Somalia
stories.summary: Uganda’s military has rejected online reports claiming its soldiers were attacked and killed in Somalia, accusing al-Shabaab of spreading propaganda. The claims surfaced during a sensitive transition: earlier in November Uganda announced a phased withdrawal from Somalia, ending nearly two decades of deployment, to be completed by the end of 2027. The UPDF and the African Union mission have been urged to publish verifiable updates on the drawdown.

stories.title: Naira depreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market as gap with official rate widens to N86.50
stories.summary: The naira weakened to N1,445 per dollar in the parallel market, widening the spread with the official rate to about N86.50. The gap has persisted despite central bank efforts to unify exchange rates and attract foreign portfolio inflows. Analysts warn the divergence keeps pressure on import costs and complicates monetary policy ahead of the November MPC meeting.

stories.title: Islamic State-linked attacks kill at least 44 civilians in eastern DR Congo
stories.summary: Gunmen from the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces killed at least 44 civilians in a series of raids across north-eastern DR Congo this week, according to humanitarian and security sources. A local official said victims were hacked with machetes and shot. The attacks in Ituri province came days after the same group killed 66 people in neighbouring North Kivu.

stories.title: Rohr’s Benin go top of AFCON 2027 qualifying group after 4-1 win over CAR
stories.summary: Former Super Eagles coach Gernot Rohr has Benin top of AFCON 2027 qualifying Group F after a 4-1 win over the Central African Republic in Abidjan. The Cheetahs face the same opponents again in Douala on 16 November, with Rohr saying a new mentality is driving the campaign.

stories.title: Fani-Kayode presents credentials to Ramaphosa as Nigeria-South Africa envoy
stories.summary: Femi Fani-Kayode has formally assumed duty as Nigeria's ambassador to South Africa after presenting his letter of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa. He pledged to rebuild relations between Abuja and Pretoria, which have been strained by diplomatic friction in recent months. The ceremony was reported by Nigerian outlets including Premium Times and ThisDay.

stories.title: Chadd Sayers backs Khawaja's sandpapergate account as Cummins denies it
stories.summary: Former Australia seamer Chadd Sayers said Usman Khawaja's account of the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering scandal is accurate, backing the opener's claim in his book Sabr that the whole Test team knew sandpaper was being used. Pat Cummins has called the claim 100 per cent wrong, and Cricket Australia defended its original investigation. David Warner publicly supported Khawaja, while Mitchell Johnson questioned the timing of the revelations.

stories.title: Jillaroos defend Women’s Rugby League World Cup with win over Kiwi Ferns
stories.summary: Australia’s Jillaroos won the 2026 Women’s Rugby League World Cup final against New Zealand at Suncorp Stadium, their fourth consecutive title. Winger Jaime Chapman scored a first-half hat-trick as Australia took control early, and captain Isabelle Kelly lifted the trophy. New Zealand’s only second-half points came through Mackenzie Wiki.

stories.title: New awards show celebrates AI music and the humans behind it
stories.summary: A new awards ceremony in Los Angeles has honoured AI-created songs and the people who make them, in an industry still divided over the technology. Organisers argue AI music is a new art form and a tool for creators, while critics point to lawsuits and complaints from artists whose work was used in training. The event drew nominees across genres and was livestreamed globally.

stories.title: Turkey and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement in Doha
stories.summary: Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani signed a mutual defence pact aimed at strengthening collective defence and regional security. The two leaders also signed agreements covering trade, energy, diplomacy, education and culture. The visit came as Gulf states weigh their response to Israel's war in Gaza and efforts to normalise Syria.

stories.title: Physicists use laser light to bring order to a crystal’s tiny electrical regions
stories.summary: Physicists at Auburn University have shown that brief flashes of laser light can align tiny electrically charged regions inside a crystal at temperatures where they would normally stay disordered. The induced order lasts about a trillionth of a second, and the team says it answers a decades-old question about how the material organises itself. The work points toward light-controlled approaches to processing and storing information.

stories.title: NC State hires Philip Rivers as head football coach
stories.summary: NC State named former Wolfpack and NFL quarterback Philip Rivers as its next head coach on a five-year deal, after its board of trustees approved the contract. Rivers, 44, replaces Dave Doeren, who was fired in October, and takes his first college coaching job after leading St Michael Catholic in Alabama since 2021. He will be introduced at a private event on Monday that airs on the ACC Network.

stories.title: S&P 500 ends volatile week at 7,561 as Nvidia slide deepens
stories.summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,561.53 on Friday, capping a week in which investors weighed a hotter inflation reading against fresh uncertainty over Nvidia's leadership. The Dow added about 0.1% while the Nasdaq was roughly flat, and the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17%, its highest since October. Nvidia shares fell 2% to $162.85 ahead of the chipmaker's earnings this week.

stories.title: Arokodare scores twice as Super Eagles bounce back with 3-1 win over Tanzania
stories.summary: Tolu Arokodare came off the bench at half-time and scored twice in eight second-half minutes as Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo to revive their AFCON qualifying hopes. Alphonce Msanga had equalised for Tanzania before Arokodare flicked home Wilfred Ndidi’s low ball and then smashed in Moses Usor’s cross.

stories.title: Nigeria issues Addis Ababa travel advisory after 16 deaths in transit
stories.summary: Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has advised travellers with pre-existing medical conditions to seek medical advice before journeys through Addis Ababa, after the embassy there recorded 16 deaths of Nigerians in transit this year linked to the city’s high altitude. At about 2,355 metres, lower atmospheric pressure reduces oxygen availability, though the ministry stressed the advisory is not a call to avoid the city.

stories.title: UN food agency chief calls for end to Sudan war as famine crisis deepens
stories.summary: The new executive director of the World Food Programme, Luke J. Lindberg, used a visit to the Goz Al-Salam camp for displaced people to call for an end to Sudan’s war and for more funding for humanitarian operations. Nearly 19.5 million people face acute food insecurity and about 825,000 children under five are expected to suffer severe acute malnutrition this year. The WFP says funding constraints forced it to cut assistance to 900,000 people and it is seeking $520 million to feed 5.4 million through April 2027.

stories.title: Burkina Faso issues arrest warrants for journalists and ex-minister
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's Ouagadougou Court of Appeal issued arrest warrants for around 20 people in exile, including RFI journalist Newton Ahmed Barry and former foreign minister Djibril Bassole. Attorney General Desire Sawadogo said 14 warrants carried extradition requests alongside seven standard warrants, with charges including complicity in forming and financing a terrorist organisation. The junta, in power since September 2022, has repeatedly targeted journalists and critics.

stories.title: Algeria sentences writer Kamel Daoud to five years over novel
stories.summary: A court in the western Algerian city of Oran sentenced Prix Goncourt winner Kamel Daoud and his wife, psychiatrist Aicha Dahdouh, to five years in prison in absentia for breaching professional confidentiality and invading privacy. The case followed a complaint from a woman who said the novel Houris used details she disclosed in therapy. Both live in France and were also fined 300,000 dinars each; Daoud called the verdict a trial without defence or justice.

stories.title: Putin agrees to let European representatives join Ukraine peace talks
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin agreed to let European representatives join the next round of Ukraine peace talks, a US envoy said, after Russia, Ukraine and the United States held a round in Abu Dhabi. The EU settled on a five-nation group to speak for Europe at the talks, while the Kremlin said it would be open to European participation if it saw genuine intent to contribute. A senior Ukrainian official said territory could be discussed only at leaders’ level and only alongside security guarantees.

stories.title: WHO greenlights two Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine candidates for Phase 2/3 trials
stories.summary: The World Health Organization’s advisory group on candidate vaccine prioritisation has recommended Phase 2/3 trials for two vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo ebolavirus species driving the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The candidates are ChAdOx1 BDBV, developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna’s mRNA-1469. WHO science director Meg Doherty said trials could begin within three to four weeks once DRC regulators approve, with initial results expected in early 2027.

stories.title: New dinosaur species identified from near-complete South African skull
stories.summary: Paleontologists have named Nyana rooiwalensis, a dinosaur that lived about 220 million years ago in what is now South Africa's Eastern Cape, from a 21.3cm juvenile skull found near Qhemegha village in 2018. Despite being roughly three years old the animal already weighed about 400kg and walked on two legs, suggesting rapid growth arose early in sauropodomorph evolution. The find is one of the most complete dinosaur skulls from this period on the southern continents.

stories.title: Kano confirms 12 diphtheria cases at First Lady’s College boarding school
stories.summary: Health authorities in Kano State have confirmed 12 cases of diphtheria at First Lady’s College in Mariri, Kumbotso Local Government Area, and tested 313 suspected cases. The outbreak was detected at the boarding school, which has more than 2,000 students, prompting the Kano State Centre for Disease Control to launch an emergency response. One student with severe symptoms was taken to the Infectious Diseases Hospital in Kano while others were treated on site.

stories.title: Dangote raises Africa investment ambition to $70bn and eyes a 10,000MW power push
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote has lifted his group’s planned investment in Africa from $50 billion to about $70 billion under its Vision 2030 strategy, with a separate 10,000-megawatt power programme across the continent that could include Nigeria. Captive generation for the group’s own plants is expected to rise from almost 1,500MW to between 4,500MW and 5,000MW.

stories.title: Naira weakens to N1,445/$ in parallel market as official gap widens
stories.summary: The naira fell to N1,445 per dollar in the parallel market, down from N1,430 the previous day, widening the gap with the official window to N86.50. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market the currency actually firmed to N1,358.50/$, so the two rates moved in opposite directions. Bureau de Change operators in Abuja attributed the parallel pressure to demand that cannot be documented through official channels.

stories.title: Reuters finds $3.2bn of Chinese AI projects built on restricted Nvidia chips
stories.summary: A Reuters review of more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans and corporate filings identified AI computing projects worth over 23 billion yuan, about $3.2 billion, specifying Nvidia's restricted H100, H200 and H800 processors. Nvidia told investors in August that US export controls had effectively shut it out of China's data-centre market, yet an IDC estimate cited by Reuters put its share of Chinese AI accelerator shipments at 34% in the first half of 2026. The records do not establish how the restricted hardware reached Chinese users.

stories.title: Nvidia sets 18 November all-hands as interim CEO Kress addresses staff
stories.summary: Nvidia will hold a company-wide meeting on 18 November at 9am Pacific, its first since Colette Kress was named interim CEO after founder Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November. Kress told employees in an internal memo that leadership would share more about the company’s future at the meeting, which lands a day after Nvidia reports third-quarter results on 17 November. Board chairman Harvey Jones said the search for a permanent CEO will consider both internal and external candidates.

stories.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases as MSF warns it is out of control
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported 10,741 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,230 deaths, with transmission active in eight provinces six months after the outbreak was declared. Médecins Sans Frontières warned on 12 November that the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record remains out of control, while WHO points to more than 2,600 recoveries and vaccine trials under way.

stories.title: PHOTOS: Palmer, three Chelsea stars receive Guinness World Records certificates
stories.summary: Four Chelsea players, including Cole Palmer and Estevão Willian, have been recognised in the Guinness World Records Football Edition 2027 for their feats.

stories.title: Two French guards collapse as Macron welcomes Slovak president
stories.summary: Two members of France's elite Republican Guard collapsed from fainting attacks outside the Elysee Palace as President Emmanuel Macron welcomed his Slovak c

stories.title: Mayweather to unveil boxing talent series in Nigeria
stories.summary: Former world boxing champion Floyd Mayweather is set to launch the TMT Frontrow Fight Series in Nigeria to discover, train and promote emerging talents.

stories.title: How poor results, dressing room rift cost Carrick Man Utd job
stories.summary: Michael Carrick's reign as Manchester United head coach has come to an end following a disappointing run of results, dressing room tensions, injury setbacks and concerns over the club's summer recruitment, according to reports.

stories.title: Man Utd confirm Carrick's sack after poor start to season
stories.summary: Manchester United have confirmed the sacking of head coach Michael Carrick following a poor start to the 2026/27 season, with just three wins in 15 matches

stories.title: Man United need bigger solution than sacking Carrick — Neville
stories.summary: Former Man United captain, Gary Neville, has warned that sacking managers like Michael Carrick will not solve the club's persistent problems.

stories.title: Ayra Starr to perform at Coachella 2027 in US
stories.summary: Nigerian singer Ayra Starr has been named among the artistes billed to perform at the 2027 edition of the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in the U

stories.title: Canada sets 18 as minimum age for adult citizenship applications
stories.summary: Canada has set 18 as the minimum age for adult citizenship applications, with separate pathways available for minors under 18, says the IRCC.
